questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Velocity has direction, so it is a vector; mass, temperature and speed are scalars (magnitude only).

questions.q: Which of these is a non-contact force?
questions.explain: A non-contact force acts without objects touching. Gravitational force acts at a distance; friction, air resistance and tension all require contact.

questions.q: Two forces act on a box along the same line: 12 N to the right and 7 N to the left. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
questions.explain: Forces along the same line subtract when opposite: resultant = 12 − 7 = 5 N (acting to the right).

questions.q: A person pushes a trolley with a force of 30 N and moves it 8.0 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done.
questions.explain: W = Fs = 30 × 8.0 = 240 J. One joule is the work done when 1 N moves through 1 m.

questions.q: A spring has a spring constant of 25 N/m. Calculate the force needed to extend it by 0.20 m (within the limit of proportionality).
questions.explain: F = ke = 25 × 0.20 = 5 N. Force is proportional to extension for an elastic spring within its limit of proportionality.

questions.q: A spanner is used to turn a nut. A force of 40 N is applied at a perpendicular distance of 0.15 m from the pivot. Calculate the moment.
questions.explain: M = Fd = 40 × 0.15 = 6 N m, where d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.

questions.q: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 0.50 m². Calculate the pressure.
questions.explain: p = F/A = 200 ÷ 0.50 = 400 Pa. Pressure is force per unit area, measured in pascals (N/m²).

questions.q: A runner completes one full lap of a 400 m circular track, finishing where they started. What is their displacement?
questions.explain: Displacement is the straight-line distance from start to finish (a vector). Finishing at the start gives 0 m displacement, even though the distance travelled is 400 m.

questions.q: On a distance–time graph, what does the gradient (slope) of the line represent?
questions.explain: On a distance–time graph the gradient equals distance ÷ time, which is the speed. A steeper line means a faster speed.

questions.q: A car accelerates from 8.0 m/s to 20 m/s in 6.0 s. Calculate its acceleration.
A spacecraft moves through deep space with its engines off and no resultant force acting. According to Newton's first law, what happens?
options: It gradually slows down and stops
It continues at constant velocity in a straight line
questions.explain: Newton's first law: with no resultant force, an object continues at constant velocity (here in a straight line at steady speed). This tendency to keep its motion is called inertia.

questions.q: A resultant force of 1200 N acts on a 400 kg go-kart. Calculate its acceleration.
A book rests on a table. The table pushes up on the book. Which is the Newton's third law pair to this force?
options: The weight of the book pulling down
The book pushing down on the table
The air pressure on the book
questions.explain: Newton's third law pairs are equal, opposite, act on different objects and are the same type of force (contact). The table pushing up on the book pairs with the book pushing down on the table.

questions.q: Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance. Which factor increases the thinking distance?
questions.explain: Thinking distance depends on reaction time, increased by tiredness, alcohol or distractions. Worn brakes, ice and bald tyres increase the braking distance instead.

questions.q: Calculate the momentum of a 0.50 kg ball moving at 8.0 m/s.
questions.explain: p = mv = 0.50 × 8.0 = 4 kg m/s. Momentum is a vector in the direction of motion.

questions.q: Calculate the weight of a 6.0 kg object on Earth (gravitational field strength g = 9.8 N/kg).
questions.explain: W = mg = 6.0 × 9.8 = 58.8 N. Weight is the force of gravity on the mass.

questions.q: An object has a resultant force of zero acting on it. What can you conclude?
options: It is either stationary or moving at constant velocity
questions.explain: Zero resultant force means no acceleration, so the object stays still or keeps moving at constant velocity (Newton's first law).

questions.q: Work is done on an object when a force makes it move. What energy transfer often warms the surroundings when work is done against friction?
options: Energy is transferred to the thermal store, raising temperature
Energy is destroyed by the friction
questions.explain: Work done against friction transfers energy to the thermal store of the object and surroundings, so they warm up. Energy is conserved, not created or destroyed.

questions.q: What does it mean if a spring is stretched beyond its limit of proportionality?
options: The extension is no longer directly proportional to the force
No more force is needed to stretch it
questions.explain: Beyond the limit of proportionality the force–extension graph is no longer a straight line, so extension is no longer directly proportional to force (and deformation may become inelastic).

questions.q: A cyclist travels 1500 m in 100 s at constant speed. Calculate the speed.
questions.explain: speed = distance ÷ time = 1500 ÷ 100 = 15 m/s.

questions.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest (u = 0) at 3.0 m/s² over a distance of 24 m. Use v² − u² = 2as to find the final speed v.
A 1500 kg car accelerates at 2.0 m/s². Calculate the resultant force needed.
questions.explain: F = ma = 1500 × 2.0 = 3000 N (Newton's second law).

questions.q: A driver's thinking distance is 12 m and braking distance is 38 m. What is the total stopping distance?
questions.explain: Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance = 12 + 38 = 50 m.
